rationale: Answers the ballot-monotonicity unknown with the master as the in-repository caller of Replica.BeTheLeader, and records that relationship in the map (B14) with two new sources. No requirement, binding, edge or identity changes; the read also notes that a promoted replica's raised ballots have not been exercised by any check, which stays as a remaining question rather than being folded into the confirmed finding.

feedback.answered: B14's unknown about what sets IsLeader is answered: the master owns that flag. At registration it marks one replica as leader - the alias named by the config's Leader field, or, when no Leader is configured, the replica with the lowest ping RTT measured by the master's ping command - and reports IsLeader to it; during master startup and again whenever its ping loop finds a leader dead, it calls Replica.BeTheLeader on the marked replica via HTTP RPC (S31-master-startup, S32-master-register). For this target that call lands in epaxos.Replica.BeTheLeader, which sets IsLeader = true and returns nil, so the master's leader/nextLeader fields stay at their defaults and the promoting replica keeps the designation. IsLeader then feeds makeBallot, which raises the ballot above maxRecvBallot while the flag is set, so a promoted replica can out-ballot anything it has seen when it recovers an instance.
remaining: whether the launched configuration sets a Leader alias at all, which decides between the configured designation and the lowest-ping-RTT choice (aws.conf was not read)

whether IsLeader = true changes the confirmed recovery finding: raising the ballot further leaves the self entry's VBallot equal to the new ballot, so the masking mechanism should persist, but no check has been run with the flag set
